questionText: In a table, what is the rectangle formed where a row and a column intersect called?
explanation: A table is made of horizontal rows and vertical columns, and the rectangles formed where they intersect are called cells. A border is the line drawn around cells.

questionText: What are Word's built-in preformatted tables, such as calendars and tabular lists, called?
explanation: Quick tables are built-in preformatted tables such as calendars and tabular lists that you can insert and edit. Table styles only change the look of an existing table.

questionText: Which Excel function finds the highest value in a range of cells?
explanation: MAX determines the highest cell value in the argument and MIN the lowest; COUNT counts cells with numerical data.

questionText: What is the default font of a new Excel workbook?
explanation: By default, the font of each new workbook is set to Calibri, though Excel offers many other fonts. Cambria is used in the Word exercises.

questionText: Which keyboard shortcut runs a PowerPoint slide show from the first slide?
explanation: Pressing F5 runs the presentation to see the effects, and Esc ends it. Ctrl+M inserts a new slide.

questionText: What are the animated effects that occur when moving from one slide to the next called?
explanation: Transitions are animated effects that happen when you move from one slide to another; animations apply to individual items on a slide.

questionText: Which Excel command lets you keep header rows visible while scrolling through data?
explanation: Freeze Panes keeps chosen rows or columns in place, shown by a gray line, while you scroll. Split divides the sheet into separately scrolling panes.

questionText: Which keyboard shortcut underlines selected text in Excel?
explanation: Ctrl+B makes text bold, Ctrl+I applies italics and Ctrl+U applies an underline. Ctrl+S saves the file.

questionText: When you insert a picture into Word, how does Word mark it by default?
explanation: Word marks an inserted picture as an embedded object by default, so it becomes part of the document and is no longer connected to the original image.

questionText: Which tab holds the Slide Master command in PowerPoint?
explanation: To create a slide master, on the View tab you click Slide Master; the slide master then appears at the top of the thumbnail pane.

questionText: How many columns can the Insert Table dialog box create at most?
explanation: The Insert Table dialog box lets you create large tables of up to 63 columns and thousands of rows by typing or using the spin box arrows.

questionText: Why should two tables inserted in a document be separated by a blank line?
explanation: When you insert more than one table in a document you should separate them with a blank line, pressing Enter below the first table, to avoid joining the tables.

questionText: What does holding Shift while dragging to draw a shape in Word do?
options: It locks Word into drawing mode
It rotates the shape as you draw
explanation: Holding Shift while clicking and dragging creates a perfect version of the selected shape. Lock Drawing Mode is chosen by right-clicking the shape in the menu.

questionText: How do you lock Word into drawing mode so that one shape can be drawn many times?
options: Right-click it in the Shapes menu, then Lock Drawing Mode
Hold Shift and click the shape in the Shapes menu twice
Double-click the Shapes button on the Insert tab
Press Esc after drawing the first shape
correctAnswer: Right-click it in the Shapes menu, then Lock Drawing Mode
explanation: Right-clicking the shape in the Shapes drop-down and choosing Lock Drawing Mode lets you draw many instances; pressing Esc cancels the lock.

questionText: What is the result of the Excel formula =5+2*8?
explanation: Multiplication is done before addition, so 2*8 = 16 and 5 + 16 = 21; calculating left to right would wrongly give (5+2)*8 = 56.

questionText: According to the order of operations, what does Excel calculate first?
explanation: Excel calculates operations in parentheses first, then exponents, then multiplication and division, and finally addition and subtraction.

questionText: How must multiple arguments in an Excel function be separated?
explanation: Multiple arguments must be separated by commas, as in =SUM(A1:A3, C1:C2, E2); a colon marks a cell range such as B1:B9.

questionText: What does the COUNT function count?
options: All non-empty cells in the range
explanation: COUNT counts the number of cells with numerical data in the argument, which is useful for counting items in a range.

questionText: How are numbers aligned in a worksheet cell by default?
explanation: By default, text is aligned to the bottom-left of a cell and numbers to the bottom-right. Alignment commands on the Home tab change this.

questionText: What must a worksheet have for filtering to work correctly?
options: A header row naming each column
A frozen first column on the left
correctAnswer: A header row naming each column
explanation: For filtering to work correctly, the worksheet should include a header row that identifies each column; drop-down arrows then appear in the header cells.

questionText: How do animations differ from transitions in PowerPoint?
options: Animations apply to items on a slide
Animations change the layout of the slide
correctAnswer: Animations apply to items on a slide
explanation: Animations apply to individual items on a slide, while transitions apply only to entire slides as you move from one to the next.

questionText: What does a small star beside a slide miniature in the thumbnail pane show?
options: A transition has been set on that slide
The slide is hidden in the show
The slide is the slide master
The slide has speaker notes attached
correctAnswer: A transition has been set on that slide
explanation: After you choose a transition effect, a small star symbol appears to the left of the slide miniature, indicating that a transition has been set up on that slide.

questionText: To freeze columns A and B, which column should you select before choosing Freeze Panes?
explanation: To freeze columns you select the column to the right of the column(s) you wish to freeze, so for A and B you select column C.

questionText: How does Sort range differ from Sort sheet?
options: Other content on the sheet is left as it is
It sorts by every column at once
It always sorts from Z to A
It removes rows that are duplicates
correctAnswer: Other content on the sheet is left as it is
explanation: Sort sheet organizes all data in the worksheet by one column, while Sort range sorts only a range of cells and does not affect other content, useful when a sheet holds several tables.

questionText: What does =AVERAGE(B1:B9) calculate?
options: The average of the values in B1 to B9
The average of B1 and B9 only
The number of cells from B1 to B9
The total of all the cells from B1 to B9
correctAnswer: The average of the values in B1 to B9
explanation: B1:B9 is a single argument meaning the range from B1 to B9; AVERAGE adds those values and divides by the number of cells. B1 and B9 alone would be written B1, B9.

questionText: Why is it best to use one transition throughout a presentation?
options: Mixed transitions distract and hurt accessibility
Mixed transitions make the file much larger
Each transition needs its own sound effect
Mixed transitions stop slide timings working
correctAnswer: Mixed transitions distract and hurt accessibility
explanation: Different transition effects between slides may add interest but distract from the talk and are not good for accessibility, so it is best to stick to one transition.

questionText: How do you standardize the transition on every slide of a presentation?
options: Choose the transition, then click Apply to All
Choose a transition on each slide one by one
Set the transition on the slide master and nowhere else
Press F5 after choosing any one transition
correctAnswer: Choose the transition, then click Apply to All
explanation: To standardize, you remove effects by choosing None and Apply to All, then choose your preferred transition and click Apply to All so every slide uses it.

questionText: How is a finished slide master saved so it can be reused as a template?
options: Save it from Slide Sorter view as a .pptx
Save it as a Quick Table
explanation: After designing the slide master, on the File tab click Save As, type a file name and in the Save as type list choose PowerPoint template, then click Save.

questionText: Which tool in Word's Screenshot menu lets you draw a box to capture only part of the screen?
explanation: The Screenshot menu shows thumbnails of open windows; choosing Screen Clipping lets you draw a box and capture an image of just its contents.

questionText: Why does PowerPoint let bullet points appear one at a time?
options: It stops the audience reading ahead
It makes the file load faster
It lets slides change automatically on a timer
correctAnswer: It stops the audience reading ahead
explanation: Showing information one item at a time stops your audience from reading ahead of you, so they concentrate on each point individually.
